title: Memory-coarsening quantization instability — follow-up and mitigation plan
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: On 2025-02-09 at ~03:14 UTC we observed a widespread degradation in hosted inference for several int8-quantized model variants. Symptoms included elevated 95th/99th latency, intermittent inference failures returning kernel error codes, and subtle generation quality drift for a subset of chat traffic. The event correlated with a gradual rollout of a quantization converter change that introduced a memory-coarsening optimization for fused attention kernels. This optimization changed buffer stride/alignment assumptions and triggered incompatible code paths on a subset of GPU drivers, causing fallback to a slower CPU path or sporadic kernel failures leading to process restarts.
timeline: 2025-02-09 02:50 UTC: Canary rollout of quant-converter v2.3.1 started (batch size 1–8).
2025-02-09 03:10 UTC: Ops alert — increase in 99th latency for hosted/text-generation on model-redwood/opt-8bit.
2025-02-09 03:14 UTC: Error spikes observed: CUDA kernel launch failures and mismatched buffer stride assertions.
2025-02-09 03:20 UTC: Canary halted; emergency mitigation: rolled back quant-converter to v2.3.0 for canary cluster.
2025-02-09 03:45 UTC: Incident declared; mitigation rollout to 20% of traffic via smart-routing fallback to float16 model variants.
2025-02-09 04:30 UTC: Full rollback initiated across affected pools; latency and error rates returned to baseline by ~04:50 UTC.
2025-02-09 06:00 UTC: Post-incident monitoring enabled; initial dive started by Quant-Infra + Runtime teams.
impact: Customer-facing: ~7% of hosted inference requests for `model-redwood/opt-8bit` experienced timeouts or errors during the 00:20–04:50 UTC window. Performance regressions increased tail latency by up to 3x for affected pods. Internally we saw ~1200 error traces aggregated and two support tickets from enterprise customers who run dedicated capacity on the affected driver versions.
root_cause: A memory-coarsening optimization in the quantization weight layout converter changed attention KV buffer stride/alignment semantics. On GPUs with specific driver/hardware combinations (NVIDIA A100 SXM with driver 525.xx) the optimized kernel assumed 256-byte alignment of per-head KV strides; however the upstream runtime's allocator produced 128-byte aligned tensors for certain batched sequences. The mismatch led to silent use of an unsupported kernel code path that either failed with kernel launch errors or forced a fallback to legacy CPU attention that increased latency and sometimes exposed quantization rounding differences (perceived as quality drift). The change was not covered by the existing regression matrix (missing combinations of driver versions and sequence length buckets) and slipped past canary because canary traffic did not exercise the relevant sequence-length/head-count distribution.
resolution: Immediate: rolled back quant-converter v2.3.1 to v2.3.0 across all affected pools and routed impacted traffic to float16 variants for tolerance. Medium-term: revert change on main branch and add a compatibility-guard in the converter to detect unsupported stride/alignment and fall back to conservative layout. Long-term: expand CI matrices, add targeted stress tests, and add a runtime assertion that emits clear telemetry when allocation alignment differs from kernel assumptions.
action_items: ENG-34121-A1: Revert memory-coarsening optimizer on main and create a guarded feature-flagged branch (owner: Jonah Kim, estimate: 2).
ENG-34121-A2: Add allocator alignment telemetry and runtime assertion for kernel stride checks; surface in Console as an alert (owner: Priya Rao, estimate: 3).

ENG-34121-A3: Expand regression CI matrix to include driver 525.xx and sequence-length buckets {128,512} and head-count permutations; add synthetic traffic generator for those distributions (owner: Sandeep Malhotra, estimate: 5).

ENG-34121-A4: Create a test harness that runs quantized attention kernels with random alignments and validates outputs against float16 baseline within per-token tolerance; integrate into pre-merge checks (owner: Quant-Infra team, estimate: 8).
ENG-34121-A5: Update rollout checklist to verify canary traffic includes long-sequence chat traces and representative head-counts; document in runtime playbook (owner: Emily Zhang, estimate: 1).
ENG-34121-A6: Reach out to enterprise customers who opened support tickets with summary and mitigation steps; Sales/CS to coordinate (owner: Jordan Mills, due: 2025-02-14).
ENG-34121-A7: Post-release canary gating: add automated downgrade-to-safe-variant policy when kernel errors exceed threshold for 2m (owner: Runtime ORCH, estimate: 3).
tests_and_metrics: Pre/post rollout metric: 99th percentile latency and kernel-error-rate per-pod (alert threshold: >0.5% kernel errors over 5m).
New unit: alignment-meter histogram (128/256/512 byte buckets) emitted from allocator to monitor drift.
Accuracy regression check: per-token log-prob delta between int8 and float16 on representative eval set; alert if >0.02 average token shift across 1k prompts.
notes: Engineering note: Quant-Infra will pair with Platform allocator owners to decide whether to change allocation alignment guarantees or to add padding in converter. The safer short-term path is padding in converter (less system-wide blast radius).

Design decision: We will not enable aggressive memory coarsening behind a global ON-by-default flag until the CI matrix and telemetry baseline are validated across all supported drivers. Feature-flagging will allow staged ramp with auto-rollback.
Process improvement: Canary traffic composition must be part of PR templates for changes that affect memory layout or kernels; add checklist item and sample generator.
